title: Superposition in disjoint variables for the infinity Laplace equation
abstract: A complete Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the three main theorems of Liu, Manfredi and Zhou, "Superposition property in disjoint variables for the infinity Laplace equation" (RIMS Kôkyûroku Bessatsu B99 (2026); arXiv:2508.17106). If u is a viscosity subsolution (resp. supersolution, solution) of -Δ∞u = f in a domain U ⊆ ℝⁿ and v one of -Δ∞v = g in a domain V ⊆ ℝᵐ, with f and g continuous, then w(x, y) = u(x) + v(y) is a viscosity subsolution (resp. supersolution, solution) of -Δ∞w = f(x) + g(y) in U × V. For a continuous, degenerate elliptic and sub-additive operator L, the sum of viscosity subsolutions of L(∇u, ∇²u) = f and L(∇v, ∇²v) = g is a subsolution of L(∇w, ∇²w) = f + g. On proper geodesic metric spaces, the disjoint sum of functions satisfying comparison with cones (from above, below, or both) satisfies comparison with cones on the product with the sum metric d_X + d_Y. Mathlib lacks the Crandall–Ishii–Lions theorem on sums, so its ingredients (sup-convolution, Alexandrov's theorem, Jensen's lemma) are formalized along the way; there is no sorry and no axiom beyond propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.
